# Uniform finite-cap envelopes and exact continuation through source ties

This note supplies analytic continuation criteria, not a new numerical depth bound. It keeps every currently deepest source and explicitly distinguishes a neutral first jet from an exact neutral path. Its motivating exact physical example is `candidate 44be6cdd33cc2f74`, independently audited in `unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.

## 1. A uniform finite-cap envelope estimate

Let K be a fixed compact subset of R^d and y0 an interior point. Let F_1,...,F_N be continuous on K times a parameter interval and continuously differentiable near (y0,0). Suppose

    F_j(y0,0)=Q,   grad_y F_j(y0,0)=-g_j,
    max_j g_j dot v >= c |v|                 (c>0),       (1)

and y0 is the unique maximizer on K of f(y,0)=min_j F_j(y,0). Let theta_j>=0 satisfy sum theta=1 and sum theta_j g_j=0. Put b_j=partial_s F_j(y0,0).

The following bounds make the estimate uniform over a family of such data. Suppose that on a fixed neighborhood of (y0,0), the first-order Taylor remainder of every F_j is bounded by

    (|v|+|s|) omega(|v|+|s|),                           (2)

where omega is nondecreasing and tends to zero at zero. Suppose also that |F_j(y,s)-F_j(y,0)|<=B|s| on K, for a common finite B>0. Choose a common radius r0>0 with omega(r0)<=c/2, and suppose

    max_(y in K, |y-y0|>=r0) f(y,0) <= Q-eta            (3)

for a common eta>0. These are quantitative assumptions; uniqueness for each member separately does not supply their uniformity.

For sufficiently small s>=0, every maximizer y_s of f(y,s) lies within r0 and satisfies

    |y_s-y0| <= 4Bs/c.                                 (4)

Indeed (1)-(2) imply f(y,0)<=Q-(c/2)|y-y0| within r0. The time-Lipschitz bound and the trial point y0 give max f(.,s)>=Q-Bs. Equation (3) excludes the exterior when 2Bs<eta. Applying the local drop at the maximizing point gives (4).

Set A=1+4B/c. Averaging the Taylor expansions with theta and using (4) gives the uniform envelope bound

    max_(y in K) min_j F_j(y,s)
       <= Q+s sum_j theta_j b_j+A s omega(A s).         (5)

The mark displacement cancels exactly. This argument does not differentiate the optimizing mark, require a unique perturbed maximizer, or interchange optimization and differentiation. If omega(r)<=Lr, its error is at most L A^2 s^2. A uniformly continuous derivative yields the stated o(s) error without a C^{1,1} assumption.

For a fixed collection of genuine cap tests through a source, (1) is positive spanning of the coarea-weighted continuous normals. A common proper own-fiber neighborhood gives the local estimates, while a complete strict finite cover supplies (3). Whether these conditions hold uniformly along a particular body path must be proved for that path. Arbitrary convex bodies are not automatically declared C^{1,1} in shape parameters.

## 2. All-source upper derivatives, including a newly tied source

Consider a continuous path of finite positive-fiber bodies on a fixed finite base P, on an interval of parameter times. Assume the candidate fibers have common compact coordinate charts and that actual normalized depth is jointly continuous in candidate and time. Thus its global maximum beta(t) is continuous. Suppose M(t)>0 is differentiable at the time under consideration.

At a fixed time t, assume that the set of all globally maximizing candidates is finite, say Y_1,...,Y_k, and each lies in its fiber interior. Around EVERY one of these candidates, choose actual through-candidate cap tests satisfying Section 1 at s=0. Write their common raw value as Q=beta(t) M(t). Let b_ij be their derivatives under the actual body path with candidate coordinates fixed, and let theta_ij be any balanced probabilities supplied by (1).

The compact complement of small neighborhoods of all Y_i has a strict actual depth gap at time t. By joint continuity this gap persists for small s. Within the neighborhoods, actual depth is bounded above by the corresponding finite cap envelope. Consequently

    D^+ beta(t)
       <= max_i {sum_j theta_ij b_ij-beta(t) M'(t)}/M(t). (6)

Here D^+ is the upper right Dini derivative. Every body-dependent smoothing width, source-coordinate chart motion, and covariance contribution must be included in b_ij. For the pure-width interface the complete b_ij is the one in `candidate 6e754f2bf13bdbd1`; dropping its covariance term changes (6).

To justify (6), use (5) at the finitely many neighborhoods, take their maximum, and divide by M(t+s)=M(t)+sM'(t)+o(s). The complement gap prevents an omitted candidate from exceeding these upper envelopes for sufficiently small s. The maximum of finitely many o(s) remainders is still o(s).

At the instant a previously inactive fiber or candidate ties for the maximum, it belongs to this list and must receive its own cap envelope. A menu selected before that instant does not automatically control it. No fixed source set along the entire path is assumed in (6).

If the right side of (6) is <=0 at EVERY t in a parameter interval, then beta is nonincreasing on that interval. This follows from the elementary Dini comparison principle: if continuous f has D^+f<=0 everywhere but f(b)>f(a), choose epsilon>0 so g(t)=f(t)-epsilon t still has g(b)>g(a). A minimum of g on [a,b] occurs at some t0<b. At that point D^+g(t0)>=0, contradicting D^+g<=-epsilon. The same argument gives beta(t)<=beta(0)-ct when D^+beta<=-c.

Thus continuation through source changes is rigorous if the ALL-current-source inequalities persist. Their availability is a geometric obligation, not a consequence of the comparison lemma.

## 3. Smooth finite-cover upper profiles

Here is one explicit source of smooth profiles for exact neutral-path arguments. Let r in R^m be body parameters near r0. At one source choose exactly d+1 cap branches F_j(y,r), all C^1 near (y0,r0), whose source gradients -g_j form a full-dimensional positive circuit. In particular the g_j are affinely independent and zero lies in the interior of their convex hull. Assume that their minimum has a unique strict global maximum y0 on the relevant compact candidate chart, and that the local gradient and global gap estimates of Section 1 hold.

The equations

    F_j(y,r)=U,  j=1,...,d+1,                            (7)

have a nonsingular Jacobian in (y,U): its rows are (-g_j,-1), and affine independence gives invertibility. The implicit-function theorem produces C^1 functions y(r), U(r). Their positive gradient circuit persists nearby. It gives a uniform strict local maximum of min_j F_j at y(r); the compact global gap excludes other maxima for r near r0. Therefore

    U(r)=max_y min_j F_j(y,r).                           (8)

In particular U is a genuine finite-cover upper bound for that fiber's actual maximum depth, not an assumed differentiability statement about the actual optimizer.

A general positive spanning menu need not contain a full-dimensional positive circuit of d+1 members: the four vectors +/-e1,+/-e2 already show this. Section 3 is therefore an additional hypothesis, not a deduction from Section 1. For larger or degenerate circuits, an independently justified C^1 upper profile may be used instead; its regularity cannot be asserted just by renaming the maximum.

## 4. Exact neutral constraint manifolds and source entry

Suppose r parametrizes an OPEN set of admissible bodies near r0. Assume M(r)>0 is C^1. For every currently deepest source choose C^1 finite-cover upper profiles U_1,...,U_k as in Section 3 or by another proved construction. Suppose all other candidate fibers have a strict depth gap near r0. Let beta0 be the actual normalized maximum at r0, and define

    G_i(r)=U_i(r)-beta0 M(r).                            (9)

If DG(r0) has row rank k, then G=0 is a local C^1 manifold of dimension m-k. Every tangent vector v in ker DG(r0) is realized by a C^1 curve r(t) through r0, with r'(0)=v and G(r(t))=0. This is the ordinary implicit-function theorem after choosing a nonsingular k-column minor and using the remaining coordinates as parameters.

For a sufficiently short part of this curve, all competing fibers remain below beta0 and all current source fibers have depth at most U_i/M=beta0. Thus the actual global depth is <=beta0 on the curve. This is an EXACT local neutral path, not merely a direction with zero first response.

However, this full-row-rank construction CANNOT apply at an actual unrestricted local minimum in an open parameter domain. Full row rank would also give a direction v with DG_i v=-1 for all i, and the same finite-cover estimates would give strict actual descent. Equivalently, the first-order alternative at a local minimum supplies lambda_i>=0, sum lambda=1, with sum lambda_i DG_i=0. The k rows must therefore be dependent. The full-rank neutral-manifold criterion is useful on nonstationary parts of a proposed path, but it is not an escape theorem for a stationary minimum.

If a new source becomes tied later along a continued path, its upper profile must be appended to (9). Continuing through that event requires admissibility, appropriate regular upper profiles, and the corresponding rank/solvability condition for the enlarged system. The earlier manifold theorem does not guarantee them. A boundary of the body-parameter domain also requires a feasible tangent construction and cannot be crossed by applying the open-domain statement.

The same framework supplies local strict descent when the k-1 tie constraints U_i-U_1=0 have full rank and their tangent space contains a vector v with D(U_1/M)v<0. Their implicit-function curve then keeps the selected source envelopes tied while decreasing the common normalized value; all other fibers remain separated initially.

No global endpoint, finite number of source changes, compact neutral component, or complexity decrease follows from these local statements. A proposed deletion strategy must separately prove such a progress mechanism. The arbitrary unequal finite-base attained counterexample shows that a purely analytic neutral-manifold argument cannot force the mixed-integer numerical target without a further arithmetic or geometric input.

## 5. The exact reduced second variation at a source tie

There is a nonvacuous tie-manifold statement at a stationary minimum, but it is second order. Assume the normalized finite-cover profiles f_i=U_i/M are C^2. Suppose the k-1 rows D(f_i-f_k), i<k, are independent at r0. Let lambda_i>=0, sum lambda=1, satisfy

    sum_i lambda_i Df_i(r0)=0.                         (10)

The affine independence of the gradients makes these lambda unique. The tie set f_i=f_k is a local C^2 manifold. Its tangent space is

    T={v : D(f_i-f_k)v=0 for every i<k}.

For v in T, all Df_i v are equal, and (10) makes their common value zero. Choose any C^2 curve r(t) in the tie manifold with initial velocity v. Such a curve exists by its local coordinate parametrization. Its common profile f(t)=f_i(r(t)) has

    f''(0)=sum_i lambda_i D^2 f_i(r0)[v,v].             (11)

Indeed differentiate each equality twice and average with lambda. The curve-acceleration contribution vanishes by (10); the remaining terms give (11). Thus this value is independent of the chosen acceleration within the tie manifold.

If the right side of (11) is negative for one admissible v, the exact tie curve gives a strict decrease of all source upper profiles, while the inactive-fiber gap persists. It is a genuine body descent. Consequently an actual unrestricted local minimum satisfying these regularity and rank hypotheses necessarily obeys

    sum_i lambda_i D^2 f_i(r0)[v,v]>=0 for all v in T.  (12)

The lambda here belongs to the SAME selected upper profiles; it is not a separator fixed across different menu choices. Equality in (11) alone does not imply an exact neutral path: higher derivatives can still increase the common value. If the rank condition on the tie equations fails, even this smooth manifold reduction needs a separate argument.

## 6. Neutral first jets do not by themselves authorize continuation

The actual mixed body in `candidate c4c8ccba329fa548` provides a useful exact warning. It has fibers rho T, epsilon h+cT, rho T at the consecutive integer bases -1,0,1, with c>rho>0 and nonzero h. The midpoint condition has strict slack, so both signs of this physical translation are admissible. After optimizing the source and all ambient cap normals, its actual raw depth satisfies

    Q(epsilon)=2(c^2+2rho^2)
          +[D(h1^2+h1 h2+h2^2)/3] epsilon^2
          +O(epsilon^3),

where D>0, while mixed mass is constant. Every first critical cap variation vanishes coherently, yet both nonzero translation directions increase the fully optimized depth to second order.

This is a genuine complete-lattice, positive-fiber example, although well above the OC target. It rules out inferring a neutral path from the affine response matrix's kernel alone. In contrast, the three-interval tie path has exact identities Q=b/2 and M=2b-a throughout its tie segment; those identities are why its continuation is valid.

# Uniform finite-cap envelopes and exact continuation through source ties

**Uniform finite-cap upper envelope under balanced gradients**

In the finite-cap envelope setting of the source, let f(y,s)=min_j F_j(y,s) on a fixed compact feasible set K, with a unique interior maximizer y0 at s=0, common active value Q, and active gradients -g_j satisfying max_j g_j.v>=c||v||. Assume the stated common exterior gap, the uniform first-order remainder controlled by omega, and the uniform time-Lipschitz bound B. For all sufficiently small s>=0, every new maximizer lies within 4Bs/c of y0, and the stated expansion has remainder bounded by A s omega(A s), with A=1+4B/c. Balanced active weights then give the certified first-order upper envelope. This is conditional on the complete finite envelope and its uniform hypotheses.

Scope limits: A conditional analytic tool. All hypotheses must be checked at the actual geometry. An optimizer need not be differentiable.

**Source-tie continuation and same-menu reduced Hessian**

Let f_i=U_i/M be the C^2 normalized source profiles in a complete attained finite envelope, and suppose the k-1 rows D(f_i-f_k) have full rank at a tie. If lambda_i>=0, sum_i lambda_i=1, and sum_i lambda_i Df_i=0, then along any tangent vector v to the exact tie manifold the common second derivative equals sum_i lambda_i D^2 f_i[v,v]. A negative value gives a local strict descent only when the source's feasible continuation and inactive-source gap hypotheses hold. The separate all-time conclusion assumes the stated continuous envelope and its upper-Dini bound.

Scope limits: Zero first or second derivative does not give a neutral path. Full-rank exact neutral constraints are impossible at an unrestricted stationary minimum; new source entries require fresh control.
